answer: Answer: GTDE-04 reports that the original arrangement did not include a carrier-beam stop preventing wedging against the top mill spreader or mill posts when backup rolls were absent. That is a reported design finding; a controlled drawing proving the absence of every possible stop has not been supplied. Evidence for the movement is GTDE-02, Reported observations: the upper beam appeared wedged against the spreader and posts; the yoke gradually moved downward over approximately two hours while the wedged carrier beam did not descend with it; relative movement displaced the beam and link arm away from the mill centerline until the link-arm stop cleared the yoke/cylinder lifting point, after which the beam fell. These records distinguish prevention of entering the interference position from retention at the link/yoke interface. Source class: controlled benchmark derivatives of partner investigation design and video findings. Limit: Original video, calibrated or annotated frames, controlled assembly drawings, tolerance stack and engineering calculations were not supplied. No supplied evidence establishes an operator bypassed a stop, or that personnel intentionally adopted wedging as a rated restraint.
